## 1. Historical Background

### 1.1 Origins and Early Development

| Year | Contributor | Contribution |
|------|-------------|--------------|
| 1949 | Donald Hebb | Hebbian learning ("neurons that fire together, wire together") |
| 1958 | Frank Rosenblatt | Perceptron, first learning machine |
| 1969 | Minsky & Papert | "Perceptrons" book, exposed limitations of single-layer networks |
| 1974 | Paul Werbos | PhD thesis: backpropagation for neural networks |
| 1982 | John Hopfield | Hopfield networks, energy-based models |
| 1986 | Rumelhart, Hinton, Williams | Popularized backpropagation in Nature paper |

### 1.2 The Key Publications

**Werbos (1974)** — "Beyond Regression: New Tools for Prediction and Analysis in the Behavioral Sciences"

- First application of backpropagation to neural networks
- Largely ignored by the machine learning community

**Rumelhart, Hinton, & Williams (1986)** — "Learning representations by back-propagating errors"

- Demonstrated that hidden layers could learn useful representations
- Showed backpropagation could train multi-layer networks
- Sparked renewed interest in connectionist models

### 1.3 The "AI Winter" and Revival

```
Timeline:
1950s-1970s: Early exploration
1969: Perceptron limitations exposed (Minsky & Papert)
1974-1986: Quiet period, backpropagation developed in parallel
1986: Rumelhart et al. popularize backpropagation
1990s: Slow progress, SVMs and kernel methods dominate
2006: Hinton's deep belief networks, "deep learning" revival
2012: AlexNet wins ImageNet, GPU acceleration
Present: Backpropagation remains the foundation of deep learning
```

---
